e.etymology: A modern spelling that can be read as Jaya, the Sanskrit word for victory, or as an American elaboration of Jay in the pattern of Mayah and Kayah.
A Latin American coinage, common in Puerto Rico, that blends Jonathan or Jonás with the -el ending of Joel and Misael.
The Italian form of Thomas, from Latin Thomas and the Aramaic word for twin, the byname of one of the twelve apostles.
Arabic matin, solid, firm and strong. Al-Matin, the Steadfast, is one of the names of God in Islam.
A respelling of Bentley, an English place name and surname from Old English beonet, bent grass, and leah, a clearing or meadow.

assoc.t: British luxury car maker, spelled Bentley

e.etymology: The spelling of Malik used in Senegal and elsewhere in French-speaking West Africa. Malik is Arabic for king; a close form, with a long first vowel, means owner or master.

A spelling of Kristof and Christoph, the Central European and Scandinavian forms of Christopher, from Greek Christophoros, bearing Christ. Disney's Frozen (2013) gave it to Anna's ice-harvester companion.
namesakes: Kristoff St. John (actor, The Young and the Restless)

assoc.t: Anna's ice-harvester companion in Disney's Frozen

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that joins Bry-, as in Bryan and Brylee, to the -lin ending.
A spelling of Halima, from Arabic halima, gentle and forbearing. Halimah al-Sadiyah was the foster mother who nursed the Prophet Muhammad.
A respelling of Jersey, the Channel Island that gave New Jersey its name. The -ey ending is Old Norse for island; the first part is disputed.

assoc.t: New Jersey, often just called Jersey

e.etymology: A spelling of Aarush, a modern Hindi name linked to Sanskrit arusha, reddish, a word for the sun and for the red horses of the fire god Agni. It is usually glossed as first ray of the sun.
Vietnamese Kiên, the Sino-Vietnamese reading of the Chinese character for firm, solid and resolute.
Arabic hamad, praise, from the same root as Ahmad, Muhammad and Hamid.
A German pet form of Anna, from Hebrew Hannah, grace, that spread north to become one of the most common names in Finland and Sweden.

e.meaning: little battler (Irish Kane); or acquired (Hebrew Cain)
e.etymology: A spelling of Kane or Cain. Kane is an Irish surname from Cathán, a pet form built on cath, battle; Cain is the biblical first son of Adam, read in Hebrew as acquired.
e.note: Sounds the same as Cain, who killed his brother Abel in Genesis.

e.etymology: An African-American coinage that puts the Da- prefix on Amauri or Amari; related spellings include Damari and Demauri.
From Arabic amir, prince or commander, with the article al-. It is a familiar name in Bosnia, Albania and Brazil.
Sanskrit sahaja, inborn, natural or easy. In Sikh teaching sahaj is the state of calm spiritual balance, which makes it a favorite Punjabi name.
A spelling of Adeline, an Old French pet form of Adela and Adele brought to England by the Normans, from a Germanic root meaning noble.
A spelling of Amina. Arabic has two close names: Amina, trustworthy, and Aminah with a long first vowel, safe and secure, the name of the Prophet Muhammad's mother. The double a marks the long vowel.
Arabic zuhra, the planet Venus and, more broadly, brightness; it shares a root with Zahra, radiant. The spelling Zohra is usual in North Africa and South Asia.
Used mostly in Latino families, alongside the spellings Esli and Hesly. Esli appears once in the Bible, as an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy.
The Italian name of Venice, the city named for the Veneti, the ancient people of the region.
A modern American coinage that reads as Ta- plus Nyla, in the pattern of Tamyra and Janyla.
The Russian name Iya comes from Greek Ias and honors Saint Ia, an early martyr; it is often linked to the Greek word for violet. Iya also means mother in Yoruba.
A Spanish-spelled form of the biblical Jeriel, a grandson of Issachar whose Hebrew name ends in El, God. It belongs to the -iel family, with Yadiel and Jadiel, popular in Puerto Rico.
The Khmer word for the sun, from Sanskrit surya, and a common Cambodian name. In the US it is also used as a variant of Soraya, the Persian name of the Pleiades.
A Latin American blend of David and Daniel, part of the -iel family that includes Yadiel and Jadiel.
A modern American name that extends Kane with the -en ending, close to Kaden and Kannon; it also resembles the biblical Cainan.
The English spelling of Sheumais, the form the Scottish Gaelic name Seumas takes when someone is addressed. Seumas is James, which goes back through Latin Iacobus to Hebrew Jacob.

e.meaning: uncertain; perhaps ice battle (Germanic) or fair to look on (Celtic)
e.etymology: The German form of Iseult, the Irish princess of the medieval romance of Tristan, fixed in this spelling by Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde. The name is either Germanic, from ice and battle, or Brythonic.
namesakes: Isolde (heroine of the Tristan and Isolde legend)

assoc.t: Tristan's doomed lover in medieval legend and Wagner's opera

e.etymology: An elaboration of Lelia or a variant of Liliana. It is best known from Leliana, the bard and spymaster of the Dragon Age video games.

assoc.t: Leliana, the bard in the Dragon Age games
